clue.text: Twenty five pounds of phosphorous about to cover yard

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top of the next piece is covering it

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A chemistry-sounding recipe: a quantity of phosphorus wrapped over a yard of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A PONY is British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a pony is a sum of £25, alongside a monkey for £500.

clue.text: US city unhappy about everything returning

indicators.note: returning says the whole result is read backwards
about says the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: unhappy means sad
everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy with the whole of an American city as they come back from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies to the whole construction, not just to everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, United States.

clue.text: Wood trade agreement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pine or fir timber, sawn into planks

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a timber trade agreement, but the wood and the agreement are two separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal names softwood planking and also a bargain struck between parties.

clue.text: Sailor up to no good creates explosion

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A mischievous sailor causing a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bang is the loud noise of a detonation, so it stands for an explosion.

clue.text: Left inept person initially moving marker?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted about into a new order
initially takes just the first letter of person

explanation.surface: A clumsy left-winger being shifted, with a hint at someone keeping score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P from person; 'moving' rearranges LEFT + INEPT + P.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is a type of marker pen; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Perjurer perhaps to protest in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rail is to protest angrily

explanation.surface: A witness who lied in court later complaining about it, looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: A perjurer tells untruths under oath, so is one example of a person who lies.

clue.text: Vault with Mexican food and bit of mescal into taxi

indicators.note: into says those pieces go inside the taxi word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a taco is a Mexican food

indicators.note: bit of takes just the first letter of mescal

explanation.surface: Taking a takeaway taco and a drop of mescal into a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives M from mescal; TACO + M goes 'into' CAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber, a kind of vault.

clue.text: Bloke in second part of The Shining regularly overcome by rapture

indicators.note: overcome by says the picked letters are covered by the joy word

parts.note: rapture means joy

indicators.note: second part of says take the second of each pair of letters, the even ones
regularly says letters are taken at a steady interval through Shining

explanation.surface: A nod to the horror film The Shining, whose famous line is 'Here's Johnny!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'second part of ... regularly' means the even-numbered letters; 'The' belongs only to the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny is informal British slang for a man or fellow, like chap or bloke.

clue.text: No noun in fancy lecture

indicators.note: No says the noun letter is absent from the fancy word

parts.note: fancy means ornate, elaborately decorated
N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher's showy lesson that never uses a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, much as one would lecture.

clue.text: Morning Heather has no coffee

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather finds there is no coffee in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a name, but it is the plant, ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a common café drink.

clue.text: Seasonal fare you will broadcast and record

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the words are replaced by a sound-alike

parts.note: you will contracts to you'll, which sounds like the word for Christmastide
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A promise that you will go on air and record something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns YOU'LL into YULE, an old word for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log is a chocolate log-shaped cake eaten at Christmas, food tied to that season.

clue.text: Expressed hesitation entering exercise ground

indicators.note: entering says the hesitation goes inside the exercise word

parts.note: to train is to exercise
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating before stepping onto a training ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features, a stretch of ground.

clue.text: Sets about turning around to keep moist

indicators.note: turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
around says the answer is found around the words, spanning sets and about

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sets about turning a roast to stop it drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no signal; 'around' does that job, with 'turning' alone for the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat or juices over meat while cooking so it stays succulent.

clue.text: Oddly boozy young man

indicators.note: Oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of boozy

explanation.surface: A young man who is strangely drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy is a male child or youth.

clue.text: Follow queens around without question

indicators.note: around signals a rearrangement of queens, and without says the question letter is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: Follow the queens around without asking anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Q out of QUEENS to leave UEENS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result, as one event may follow another.

clue.text: Runner descending slope almost full pelt

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the pelt word is lost

parts.note: a full pelt is a whole skin

explanation.surface: Someone skiing downhill at full pelt, almost out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full pelt' looks like the idiom for top speed, but here pelt is an animal hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Teams on plane perhaps with time to find less congested path

parts.note: sides are teams
the plane is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: Sports teams flying on a plane, finding a quieter route.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane looks like an aircraft; it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A side street is a minor road off a main one, carrying lighter traffic.

clue.text: Agent in favour of facing unknowns

parts.note: pro means in favour of
x and y are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: An agent who supports facing up to the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a person authorised to act for another, a representative.

clue.text: Prop up ill-prepared boxing student

indicators.note: boxing says the words enclose the answer, the letters spanning prop, up and ill

explanation.surface: Propping up an unready student boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is someone being taught, a learner at school.

clue.text: Affirmative answers the jury ultimately returns

indicators.note: returns says those final letters are read backwards
ultimately takes the final letter of each of answers, the and jury

explanation.surface: A jury finally comes back with a positive verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S, E, Y; 'returns' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes is the word of agreement, an affirmative reply.

clue.text: Argument about unfinished hat and shoe

indicators.note: about says the argument word goes round the trimmed hat

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or argument

indicators.note: unfinished says the hat word loses its last letter

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A row over an unfinished hat and a shoe, as in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat; SET-TO, a fight, is the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a women's shoe with a very thin high heel.

clue.text: Obnoxious person takes a shot with soft drink

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person
a pop is a shot, as in taking a pop at someone

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person knocking back a shot with a mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda pop is a fizzy non-alcoholic drink, mainly American usage.

clue.text: Bounce backwards and forwards

indicators.note: backwards and forwards says the answer to Bounce reads the same in either direction

parts.note: to bounce up and down; the same word is then read both ways

explanation.surface: Something bouncing to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like more of the motion, but it says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move up and down quickly, as a cork bounces on water.

clue.text: Club Bill returned

indicators.note: returned says the bill word is read backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A club sends back the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is a club used in cricket or baseball to strike the ball.

clue.text: King leaving wicket destroyed more than once

indicators.note: leaving says the king letter departs from the pool of letters
destroyed says the letters of wicket are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A batsman-king walks off after his wicket is smashed again.
explanation.walkthrough: Take K out of WICKET to leave WICET, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice means two times, which is more than a single occasion.

clue.text: Cheap American couple taking a while

definitions.note: the definition is the American slang sense of cheap or trivial

parts.note: a couple is two
a bit is a while, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: An American skinflint and his partner taking their time.
explanation.walkthrough: Two-bit, from the American quarter dollar called two bits, is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is American slang for worthless or petty, of little value.

clue.text: Uniform sporting tin star

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the tin symbol has the uniform letter on it, inside

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tin star sheriff dressed in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

clue.text: Lawful boundary having mile removed for Conservative

indicators.note: removed for says the mile letter is taken out and the Conservative letter put in its place

parts.note: a limit is a boundary

explanation.surface: A lawful border with a mile handed over to a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means permitted by law, the opposite of illicit.

clue.text: Wail about that woman's fruit

indicators.note: about says the cry word wraps round the possessive

parts.note: to wail is to cry
her means belonging to that woman

explanation.surface: Someone wailing over a woman's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round stone fruit.

clue.text: Dancing in opera outside

indicators.note: dancing has the letters moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dancers performing in an opera staged outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outdoors rather than in a building.

clue.text: Join anonymous objection

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Someone joining in with an unsigned complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to be adjacent to and touch, so two things abutting are joined.

clue.text: Characters Liberal setter disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed says the word setter is thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled crossword setter of liberal views.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters are the written symbols of the alphabet, its characters.

clue.text: US city with way to survive

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An American city and a way to survive there.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to endure or keep going, as a survivor does.

clue.text: Riding gear and whip upended by knight

indicators.note: by means next to, so the knight letter sits beside the reversed whip
upended in a down clue means the whip word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: the cat, cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Horse tack and a whip knocked over by a mounted knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is the saddles, bridles and other equipment used on horses.

clue.text: Baby cows regularly rejected protein

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the picked letters are read backwards
regularly takes every other letter of baby cows, the even ones

explanation.surface: Calves refusing a dairy substitute protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives AYOS; 'rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is a bean that is a major plant source of protein for food.

clue.text: Trespassers stupidly sit under opening in roof

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters are jumbled in a foolish way
opening in takes the first letter of roof

explanation.surface: Intruders foolishly sitting beneath a hole in the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from roof joins the fodder before the shuffle, not after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Intruders enter without permission, which is what trespassers do.

clue.text: Shortly dismissing head of team with waves

indicators.note: dismissing says that letter is sent out of the curt word

parts.note: shortly can mean curtly, rudely brief

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of team

explanation.surface: A team captain being briefly fired, with a wave goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly looks like 'soon', but means curtly; drop the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly hair has curls or waves in it, so it is wavy.
